caption:
What does sunscreen actually do for ageing, and is it worth the fuss?
More than almost anything I can offer you in a chair.

Treatments and daily protection do two different jobs. One works on what has already happened. The other works on what has not happened yet. Most people buy the first and skip the second, and the order matters, because you can always add a treatment later but you cannot go back and un-spend the years.

A trial followed 903 adults for four and a half years. The group using broad-spectrum sunscreen daily showed 24% less skin ageing than the group using it when they felt like it - and no detectable increase in ageing at all. Groups were randomly assigned, so this is not a survey of people who already look after their skin.

One check this week: notice where your face actually spends the day. Not the beach - the window seat, the drive, the desk. Glass stops burning, not ageing.

General education only.

#SunProtection #SkinAgeing #KoreanAesthetics #MedicalAesthetics #BetterDecisions
first_comment: The honest catch: this one has no before-and-after. Prevention looks like nothing happening, which is exactly why it gets skipped. Where does your face spend most of its day?

slides.alt_text: Slide 1 of 6: A plain white tube and a mirror on an oak desk, half in sunlight. The most effective thing is not a treatment.
Slide 2 of 6: Three cards - already there, not yet there, the usual order. One removes, one prevents, most people skip one.
Slide 3 of 6: Twenty-four percent less skin ageing over four and a half years with daily sunscreen, from a randomised trial.
Slide 4 of 6: The one-week check - map the light, check the glass, find the gap. Where does your face spend the day?
Slide 5 of 6: Four things daily protection will not do, including erasing what is there and replacing a diagnosis.
Slide 6 of 6: Cost, effort and result of the part that never stops working. The result is nothing, and that is the point.
